articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip in children born in England and Wales.
articles.population: Children born in England and Wales
articles.outcomes: Cost per quality-adjusted life-year gained; incremental net monetary benefit; clinical effectiveness of six screening programmes
articles.take_home: The current NHS screening approach of clinical examination followed by ultrasound only for babies with abnormal findings or risk factors is the most cost-effective way to screen for hip dysplasia. Universal ultrasound screening finds more cases but costs much more money without enough benefit to justify the extra expense.

articles.title: Dwarf Maiden of Acropolis.
articles.authors: Rebello G, Shah H, Joseph B
articles.population: Marble sculpture depicting a dwarf maiden from the Acropolis
articles.outcomes: Identification of disproportionate rhizomelic dwarfism based on statue features
articles.take_home: Analysis of an ancient Greek marble sculpture suggests it represents a person with disproportionate rhizomelic dwarfism, making it a historically significant depiction of a dwarf among many other statues in the Athenian Acropolis.

articles.title: Antihistamines for atopic dermatitis (eczema): systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials.
articles.authors: Chu AWL, Wen A, Guyatt GH, Rao M, Bakaa L, Zhao IX, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials
articles.population: Children and adults with primarily moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (eczema)
articles.outcomes: Atopic dermatitis severity, itch severity, sleep disturbance, quality of life, and adverse effects including cognitive impairment
articles.take_home: Adding antihistamines to eczema treatment produces only small reductions in severity and itching that are too small to matter to patients, and they do not help with sleep or prevent flare-ups. First generation antihistamines can affect thinking and concentration, so second generation options may be safer if antihistamines are used.

articles.title: Femoral anterior distal hemiepiphysiodesis for correction of knee flexion contractures in arthrogryposis.
articles.population: Children with arthrogryposis and knee flexion contractures
articles.outcomes: Knee range of motion, ambulatory ability, contracture recurrence. Mean contracture improved from 35 degrees to 7 degrees at hardware removal (average 17.5 months). 16 of 31 non-ambulatory patients became independent walkers. Overall recurrence rate 0.61 degrees per month; 9 patients required repeat surgery.
articles.take_home: Femoral anterior distal hemiepiphysiodesis is effective for treating knee contractures in children with arthrogryposis, particularly when contractures are 25 degrees or less, or up to 55 degrees when combined with posterior release. Although contractures can recur, this is treatable with repeat surgery and orthotic bracing.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Mechanical Failure of Noninvasive Expandable Prostheses: A Retrospective Service Evaluation of a UK Health Service.
articles.authors: Bertelli L, O'Keeffe R, Bruni K, Ampiah PK
articles.population: Paediatric bone tumour patients who received noninvasive expandable prostheses at the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital
articles.outcomes: Mechanical failure rate (defined as lengthening mechanism stopping) and factors influencing failure risk, including anatomic location and lengthening variables
articles.take_home: Overall, 38% of expandable prostheses experienced mechanical failure, with total femoral and femoral diaphyseal replacements having significantly higher failure rates than distal femoral replacements. The location of the implant in the leg appears to be the main factor influencing whether the prosthesis will fail mechanically.
